caption:
READ THIS when I say “don’t pick a niche”, that doesn’t mean don’t have an anchor to your content.

You bascially have two options (or a hybrid of both.) 

 ONE: 
Lead with expert content. That means your niche, for want of a better word, would become your anchor topic. This is what my account is mostlyyyy doing in the way that I’m talking about social media a lot. I’m creating synergy between personal branding and my face. 

It means that my goal is when you’re sitting at dinner and someone starts talking about social media, you reference the girl in the matcha hat that has been popping up on your feed all week. 

BUT notice what else you know about me (50k follower bet, loves matcha, lives in cape town, has cocker spaniel etc). You’re allowed to have an anchor subject and still know and still reference things wider about who you actually are as a human! 

TWO: 
You lead with a journey perspective. 
So, you have to give someone the narrative of who you are and where you’re trying to get to. 

Is it that you’re a new mum and you’re trying to fit all of the things in your world into your new time schedule? Is it that you’re in your thirties and suddenly realising that you don’t want to do the career that you signed up to do for the rest of your life? Are you testing or trying new hobbies to figure out how to funmaxx your life? 

THREE: 
My personal favourite is usually both (especially if you’re trying to sell something, a service or coaching etc). That’s exactly why I have this 50,000 followers bet with Patrick on this account, because it creates this fun entertainment aspect that I get to joke about constantly. 

Which are you - expert, journey or both? 

PS. Doing a full breakdown of this in tomorrow’s free masterclass. Comment “reset” if you want to nab one of the final spots!

transcript: Female founders should not pick a niche. I said what I said. For years, the old advice was pick a niche, stay in your lane, and it created a generation of creators who are so fucking bored of their own content. Here's what actually works to make a personal brand in 2026. You're gonna want to hit save because I want you to go away and immediately action this. You're gonna take a pen and paper, you're gonna write down what do you think about every day, what do you talk to your friends about, what do people know you for, what could you talk about for two hours without any notes, what are you currently going through in your life. That list, that is your fucking personal brand. Not a topic, not a category, not a niche. You believe that I want to help as many women as possible get a personal brand because it opens up this whole world of opportunities that opens up a whole world of independence and how you show up for your family and how you're able to look after your health and you cycle your hormones. Personal brand is going to empower all of that. But I'm not just talking about social media and my content. I cycle sync everything. I moved from London to Cape Town three years ago. I'm growing an Instagram account from zero in public. I care about my hormones and habits and building a business that does not cost me my health. That combination of things is what people follow because now you know something about me, not just my content tips and isolation. You've connected to me. Say it one more time, people do not connect to niches, they connect to a human with perspective. So you are the niche. So stop figuring out what you need to post and start being exactly what you already are. It's so much easier than you think. A couple of posts ago, I broke down exactly how to action across the next three and a half months so that you're sitting in August and going, oh, fuck, I grew a personal brand and it actually started to have an impact that quickly. Go back and look at it. It's going to help you.
title: You Are the Niche: Personal Brand Strategy
one_liner: Stop picking a niche — build a personal brand around who you are, not a topic.
key_points: Lead with expert content (anchor topic) OR a personal journey narrative — or combine both for maximum connection
People connect to humans with perspective, not to niches or content categories
Your real brand is what you think about daily, talk to friends about, and could discuss for hours without notes
Mixing expertise with personal narrative (e.g., a public growth bet) adds entertainment and drives deeper audience loyalty
